call_points.text: Railway Sub-systems & Defense guided to 30-35% revenue growth in FY27, with margins of 15-16%.
Consumer durables to grow 13-15%, in line with industry; no EBITDA margin percentage guidance given.
Earlier 50-100 bps full-year margin decline guidance dropped; margins seen normalised at current level absent further commodity or currency disruption.
PCB margins at about 12% versus a normal 16%; recovery expected from Q3, subject to no further CCL price rises.
Three ECMS approvals received: ₹3,200 Cr Jewar HDI PCB, ₹1,000 Cr Hosur, ₹500 Cr Shogini Pune.
Net debt rose to about ₹1,225 Cr at 30 June from ₹510 Cr at March 2026.
ILJIN fundraise is an enabling board resolution of up to ₹5,000 Cr; quantum and form not yet decided.
ILJIN fire: reconstruction permission received; loss being assessed, business shifted to other locations, and the division's guided numbers expected to be met.
EMS growth was stunted by customer inventory and a shift from sales to job work; smart meter and smart watch segments degrew.
Initial capex for assembly and SMT is below ₹50 Cr, with no capex for the subleased facility.
Trial production expected in Q4FY27 and commercial production in Q1FY28, with the first three months treated as a learning curve.
Management expects ROCE of more than 30-35% on a standalone basis for this business.
Working capital is described as minimal, with the sector operating at 4-5 net working capital days, maximum 10.
The agreement covers three brands: Oppo, OnePlus and Realme; no arrangement with Vivo at present.
Amber now owns 98.5% of Ascent, up from 60%; the PCB division is headed by Santosh, formerly of AT&S.
Management declined to comment on the second PLI scheme until a draft notification is available.
The entity structure (Amber or IL JIN) and gross versus job-work revenue recognition are not yet decided.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has engaged a legal firm to file a writ petition in the High Court. The draft of the petition has been finalized and is scheduled to be filed by the second week of November 2025
tax_litigation.status: Considering the Show Cause Notice legally untenable the Company filed a writ petition before the Honble High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad challenging its validity The Honble High Court observed that the impugned Show Cause Notice did not comply with the prescribed verification procedures mandated under the applicable statutory framework including the Customs Administration of Rules of Origin under Trade Agreements Rules 2020 ie CAROTAR as the requisite verification of preferential duty claims had not been undertaken prior to issuance Consequently by its order dated 19th January 2026 which was received by the Company on 20th January 2026 the Honble High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad directed that all further proceedings arising from the Show Cause Notice be stayed until the next date of hearing Accordingly the Company has formally received a Stay Order from the Honble High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in connection with the said Show Cause Notice

tax_litigation.status: The Show Cause Notice dated 28 February 2025 was heard by the Honble High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad on 19 June 2026 During the hearing the Company submitted that identical matters are presently pending before the Honble Supreme Court of India in Special Leave Petitions filed against the judgment of the Honble High Court of Delhi whereby writ petitions challenging similar show cause notices had been dismissed The Company further apprised the Honble Court that notices have been issued by the Honble Supreme Court in the said matters which are presently listed for hearing on 27 July 2026 In view of the pendency of the aforesaid proceedings the Company requested that the present matter be taken up after the issue is considered by the Honble Supreme Court Taking note of the submissions made by the Company the Honble High Court of Gujarat vide its order dated 19 June 2026 adjourned the matter and listed it for further hearing on 06 August 2026 The ad interim relief granted earlier shall continue until the next date of hearing

tax_litigation.status: The matter was listed for hearing on 06 August 2026 before the Honble High Court of Gujarat wherein the Honble Bench adjourned the proceedings and listed the matter for further hearing on 25 August 2026 The Honble Court further directed that the ad interim relief granted earlier being the stay on all proceedings arising from the Show Cause Notice would continue until the next date of hearing Thereafter the matter was heard on 25 August 2026 upon which the Honble Bench adjourned the proceedings and listed the matter for further hearing on 22 October 2026 while continuing the aforesaid ad interim relief On 22 October 2026 the matter was taken up for hearing and was listed for further hearing on 01 December 2026 The ad interim relief granted earlier continues to remain in force until the next date of hearing

operating_notes.text: Amber Enterprises invested ₹296.02 Cr to subscribe to 12,46,430 equity shares in material subsidiary IL JIN Electronics' rights issue, taking total holding to 60,98,240 shares.
Q4FY26 exceptional item of ₹64.02 Cr relates to incremental gratuity and long-term compensated absences from the new Labour Codes.
Railway division order book stood at over ₹2,600 crores as of May 2026.
Material subsidiary IL JIN Electronics incorporated ILJIN Technologies Private Limited as a 60% step-down subsidiary with ₹0.60 Cr subscription.
NCLT Chandigarh Bench approved First Motion Application for amalgamating wholly owned subsidiary AmberPR Technoplast into Amber Enterprises.
Amber's IL JIN unit already makes 9-10 million smart watches a year and about 15 million PCB assemblies, and the group makes more than 5.5 million air conditioner boxes a year.
The mobile manufacturing facility is an existing Oppo India compound subleased with exclusivity arrangements; no Press Note 3 approval is required.
Industry EBITDA for mobile assembly is 1.5-2% excluding PLI, and net working capital is 4-5 days, maximum 10 days.
PCB margins were about 12% in Q1FY27 against a normal 16%, with recovery expected from Q3FY27 subject to no further copper clad laminate price increases.
Consumer durables revenue mix is roughly 75% RAC (finished goods plus components) and 25% non-RAC, with pure RAC around 55-60%.
PCB asset turns are about 0.8:1, with ₹3,200 Cr announced at Jewar and about ₹1,000 Cr at Hosur.

timeline.summary: Amber Enterprises completed a ₹296.02 Cr investment in subsidiary IL JIN Electronics via rights issue, taking holding to 60,98,240 shares.

Amber Enterprises India Limited scheduled an Earnings Call on May 18, 2026, at 9:30 AM IST to discuss Q4 & FY2026 audited results with Mr. Jasbir Singh, Mr. Daljit Singh, Mr. Sudhir Goyal, and Mr. Ravi Kharbanda.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,147.52 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹133.88 Cr.
Amber Enterprises India Limited uploaded the earnings call audio for Q4 & FY2026 results discussion held on 18 May 2026 at 09:30 AM IST via its IR website.
Amber Enterprises held its Q4 and FY26 earnings call on May 18, 2026, reporting a 22% jump in consolidated revenue to ₹12,186 Cr.
Amber Enterprises' material subsidiary IL JIN incorporated a 60% subsidiary, ILJIN Technologies, for medical and aerospace electronics with a ₹0.60 Cr capital infusion.
On June 5, 2026, the NCLT Chandigarh Bench approved the dispensation of meetings for the amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary AmberPR Technoplast into Amber Enterprises.
On 20 June 2026 Amber held a business update call on its manufacturing collaboration agreement with Oppo Mobiles India, executed 18 June, targeting 8-9 million units in year 1 from Q1FY28.
IL JIN Electronics entered into a Share Swap Agreement to acquire the remaining 1.5% stake in Ascent Circuits, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.
IL JIN Electronics entered a Share Swap Agreement on October 18, 2026, to acquire the remaining 40% stake in Power-One Micro Systems.
